reason: The text features multiple regular people who display genuine agency. Most notably, Arnan (אָרְנָן הַיְבוּסִי - the Jebusite) is a private citizen who makes independent decisions: he hides when he sees the angel, then chooses to come forward, respectfully bows to David, and actively negotiates the terms of selling his threshing floor to David. Similarly, Joab (David's commander) demonstrates agency by initially objecting to the census before carrying it out, and David himself makes choices throughout (ordering the census, repenting, negotiating with Arnan). These are not passive characters but individuals who take actions and make decisions that drive the narrative forward.
